summary: @c1-ease/card ships a postinstall and import-time beacon exfiltrating host identifiers to a hardcoded VPS
details: The package is a stub exporting a Proxy of no-op functions with no advertised functionality. Its package.json postinstall runs `node beacon.cjs`, which POSTs installer host identifiers (hostname, install path, cwd, node version) to the hardcoded endpoint https://vmi3699893.contaboserver.net:8787/_ah/dc with TLS verification disabled (`rejectUnauthorized: false`). The main entry `index.js` additionally calls `require('./beacon.cjs').fire()` at load time, so every `require('@c1-ease/card')` re-sends the same host identifiers to the same bare-VPS endpoint. The version `99.0.1` on the `@c1-ease` scope paired with a `Compatibility shim.` description and a Proxy-no-op cover is consistent with a dependency-confusion probe against an internal package of the same name.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
